rounds.text: S V Global Mill Ltd demonstrates robust multi-year top-line expansion, highlighted by compounded sales growth of 20% over 5 years and 17% over 3 years [E13, E14]. This momentum persists through the trailing twelve months with a 14% increase in sales [E15], supported by a recorded multi-year sales uptrend and quarter-on-quarter sales growth [E61, E62]. Furthermore, the operating margin shows structural long-term improvement, rising by 110 percentage points from -409% three years ago to -299% in Mar 2026 [E25]. Relative valuation also presents an attractive entry point compared to the broader industry, as the company's price-to-book ratio of 4.51x sits comfortably below the sector benchmark of 6.18x [E6]. Conceded: trailing profit growth stands at -3278% with quarterly margins contracting year-on-year, and return metrics like ROE and ROA lag behind sector benchmarks [E7, E8, E16, E26].

The valuation of S V Global Mill Ltd is fundamentally disconnected from its underlying operational reality, trading at a price-to-book ratio of 3.41x [E1] and a trailing P/E of 37.63x, which sits above the sector benchmark of 33.36x [E5]. This premium pricing is entirely unjustified given the catastrophic destruction of shareholder value, highlighted by an abysmal return on equity (ROE) of -48.31% against a sector benchmark of 5.76% and a return on assets (ROA) of -16.06% compared to a sector benchmark of 1.44% [E7, E8]. Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has collapsed by -3278% [E16], resulting in a severe earnings deceleration and a quarterly operating margin of -302% in March 2026 [E26]. Expectations are dangerously detached from delivery, with price growth exceeding profit growth by an alarming 3257% [E52], while the stock languishes at just 12% of the way up its 52-week range [E4] and offers zero dividend yield at 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 5 years is 20% [E13].

While the bear highlights a premium P/E of 37.63x [E5] and negative returns on equity and assets [E7, E8], the market actually prices this asset below its sector peers on a relative basis with a price-to-book of 4.51x against a sector benchmark of 6.18x [E6]. Conceded: the trailing twelve months show a compounded profit growth drop of -3278% [E16] and a quarterly operating margin of -302% [E26]. However, focusing solely on trailing distress ignores the powerful multi-year top-line momentum, driven by a 20% compounded sales growth over 5 years and 17% over 3 years [E13, E14]. This structural revenue expansion is further reinforced by positive screen reasons showing sales up QoQ and a multi-year sales uptrend [E61, E62]. Finally, the long-term operational trend shows structural repair, with the operating margin improving by 110 percentage points from -409% to -299% [E25].

Conceded: the price-to-book of 4.51x sits below the sector benchmark of 6.18x [E6], and the operating margin shows a multi-year improvement of 110 percentage points from -409% to -299% [E25]. However, the bull's reliance on top-line momentum via 20% 5-year and 17% 3-year sales growth [E13, E14] is completely detached from the company's financial reality, given that trailing twelve months profit growth has plummeted by -3278% [E16] and quarterly sales actually dropped -9% YoY [E63]. Furthermore, pointing to QoQ sales increases or multi-year uptrends [E61, E62] ignores the staggering operational collapse reflected in the quarterly operating margin diving further to -302% in Mar 2026, down 122 percentage points from the year-ago quarter [E26]. The claim of structural revenue expansion is entirely undermined by catastrophic bottom-line destruction and deeply negative returns, with ROE sitting at -48.31% and ROA at -16.06% against sector benchmarks of 5.76% and 1.44% respectively [E7, E8]. Finally, paying a premium P/E of 37.63x [E5]—which exceeds the sector benchmark of 33.36x—for a business where price growth has outpaced profit growth by 3257% [E52] is a dangerous disconnection from fundamentals, especially when the stock is trapped near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 12% of the way up [E4] and yields a dead 0.00% dividend [E3].
